1. Diversification matters
A well-diversified portfolio across different sectors, companies and asset classes can reduce the impact of a sharp fall in any single part of the market. It does not eliminate losses, but it can help manage concentration risk.
2. Don't be afraid of market corrections
Market corrections are a normal part of investing. A falling market can be uncomfortable, but for a long-term investor it can also create opportunities to invest additional money at lower valuations—provided the underlying investments remain suitable for the investor's goals and risk tolerance.
